newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Menem denies 1999 re-election bid.
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Menem denies 1999 re-election bid.

text.p: Argentine President Carlos Menem denied once more this weekend that he would try to run for a third consecutive term in 1999.
The denial followed fresh speculation sparked by Menemist Senator Jorge Yoma's plans to legalise plebiscites to allow the constitution to be changed.

"I determined long ago to have nothing to do with this re-election game because I have completed a cycle," said Menem during a weekend at a country estate, in comments reported by the local media on Sunday.
The Peronist president was first elected in 1989, then re-elected with 50 percent of the vote in 1995 after changing the constitution a year earlier to allow a second term.

Menem is frequently obliged to deny reports that he will seek re-election in 1999, though he does talk of seeking another term in 2004, after one term out. But fiercely loyal Peronist activists put up "Menem '99" banners each time there is a Peronist Party conference.

Yoma sparked the latest speculation by announcing on Friday he would launch a bill in Congress in February to give legal status to plebiscites. Such plebiscites would exclude no issues, not even reforming the constitution, the Peronist senator said. This was interpreted as a sign he wants to change statutes that currently block Menem from running again.

But the president said this should not be read into the senator's proposed bill. This line was underscored on Sunday by Interior Minister Carlos Corach, who said the only reason for seeking legal status for plebiscites was for cases such as the current controversy over labour reforms.
